FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: borscht with smetana
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} grated and sharpened with vinegar so as to hold their red — without acid the soup turns brown — with {1_coll}, and a spoonful of {2_adj} that draws pink spirals as it melts.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bigos
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} fermented and fresh mixed together, stewed with {1_plur} and dried {2_plur}, then cooled and reheated several days running. They say it is only good at the third reheating.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: blini
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small {0_adj} pancakes raised with yeast and left to swell for hours, cooked in butter and served warm with thick {2_plur}. Late-winter feast food, eaten for a week at a time.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coulibiac
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} in one whole piece, {1_coll} and hard-boiled {2_coll} built up in strata inside a closed brioche and baked together. Cut like a terrine, and it reveals its layers all at once.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: solyanka
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a soup deliberately sour and salt: {0_coll} of several kinds, {1_coll} pickled and put in with their brine, {2_coll} and a slice of lemon. The dish of the morning after, and that is no accident.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: vareniki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: half-moons of dough filled with crushed {1_plur}, poached and then doused with {2_adj} melted down in butter. The seal has to hold in boiling water: that is the whole craft.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: khachapuri
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a bread shaped like a boat filled with melted {1_adj}, with a raw yolk and a knob of {2_adj} set at the centre as it leaves the oven. Everything is mixed together with the tip of the crust, torn off for the purpose.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: plov
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {2_coll} cut into long batons — never grated — sweated with {1_plur} and its fat, {0_coll} poured over without being stirred in and cooked in the steam from below. Made in a cauldron, for fifty people.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: shashlik
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated overnight with grated {1_plur} and {2_plur}, threaded onto broad metal blades and grilled over dying embers. A lean piece, then a fat piece, and so on.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kasha
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} toasted dry until it smells of hazelnut, then swelled in salted water and generously {1_plur}, with {2_coll}. The most ordinary dish there is, and the one most missed when you leave.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: żurek
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a white and frankly sour soup, built on a {0_adj} leaven fermented for several days, with smoked {1_coll} and hard-boiled {2_coll}. Sometimes served in a hollowed loaf, which is eaten at the end.
